evidence.claim: Each of four corruption modes (truncated, wrong_hash, unreadable_permissions, leftover_tmp) is classified by a named detector, quarantined, and rebuilt; IntegrityCache did not serve corrupt bytes.

Cache publish is tmp+os.replace: an interrupt before replace leaves no partial on entries/<key>/; in-place-write mutant DOES leave a readable partial so the detector is not silent in both states. Rebuild payload sha256 matches render(source).

negative_controls.description: SilentServeCache returns on-disk bytes without integrity checks. Detector must fire (served_corrupt=true) on the mutant and stay silent on IntegrityCache.
InPlaceWriteCache writes a truncated payload onto the publish path. inspect() must classify it; IntegrityCache interrupt-before-replace must not publish a partial.
An intact planted entry is a hit: not quarantined, not rebuilt, payload sha256 matches. Proves the detector is silent on the good state.

report.claim_under_test: A cache that publishes with tmp+os.replace and verifies payload length, mode bits, and sha256 on read will detect truncated, wrong-hash, unreadable, and leftover-tmp corruption, quarantine the bad object, and rebuild a correct entry. Serving corrupt bytes is a P0 and did not occur on IntegrityCache.
report.question: Phase 10 layer 25. Target: corrupt the cache in each distinct way (truncated entry, wrong hash, unreadable permissions, half-written temp file left behind) and assert the system detects and rebuilds rather than serving corrupt data. Precedent: a render cancelled mid-write can leave a half-file unless writes are atomic (tmp + mv -f).

silent_serve_p0.control: mutant returns on-disk bytes without checks; IntegrityCache never does
